clue.text: A loose coin rattles, occasioning some cross words

indicators.note: set loose, the letters of the words that follow are freed to fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A jingling pocketful of change sets off an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A stands as written; 'loose' rearranges 'coin rattles' to give the rest. 'occasioning' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross words are angry exchanges, and a heated quarrel is exactly such a dispute.

clue.text: After midnight draw on a flask

parts.note: AM marks the hours after midnight
to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: In the small hours someone takes a swig from a hip flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampulla is a small two-handled flask, as the Romans or churches used for oil.

clue.text: Stuff to sample without hesitation

indicators.note: here in its old sense outside, so the word for sample sits around the hesitation

parts.note: to try is to sample or taste
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Some food to taste without pausing first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. 'Stuff' is a noun: an old word for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for cloth, and this looped cotton fabric is used for towels.

clue.text: The odd athlete evading his duty?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the person who avoids paying customs duty

parts.note: rum is a British informal word for odd or strange
a runner is an athlete

explanation.surface: A strange sportsman is shirking his obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' looks like obligation; it is customs duty on alcohol. 'The' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler of alcohol avoids customs tax, as bootleggers did in Prohibition times.

clue.text: A vessel capsized end on

indicators.note: overturned, as in a down clue the word for vessel is turned upside down

parts.note: a tub is a vessel, both a container and slang for a boat

explanation.surface: A boat has overturned bow first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns TUB to BUT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin something end on is to border it, touching at one end.

clue.text: Space travel in formation

indicators.note: a formation is a new arrangement, so the letters of the words are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spaceships flying in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges TRAVEL and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap or pause between two things is a space, in time or distance.

clue.text: In the main one thoroughly enjoys such music

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone in the open sea enjoys this music to the full.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across maiN ONE Thoroughly; 'enjoys' and 'the' are links. 'In the main' looks like 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for nine players or voices is named from the Latin for ninth.

clue.text: A deterrent for compulsive eaters in the cupboard

definitions.text: A deterrent for compulsive eaters in the cupboard

parts.words: A deterrent for compulsive eaters in the cupboard
parts.note: the eaters are not dieters raiding the pantry but insects chewing woollens in the wardrobe, kept off by a camphor ball

explanation.surface: Something to stop greedy people raiding the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compulsive eaters' suggests binge eaters; they are clothes moths.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ball of naphthalene or camphor is stored among clothes to repel insects.

clue.text: Tender grub

definitions.meaning: an old word for a maggot used as fishing bait

explanation.surface: Soft food.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the angler's maggot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild and kind means soft-hearted, and anglers once called a blowfly maggot by this name.

clue.text: Back strike — a rise is most important!

indicators.note: placed before the word for strike, it tells us to write that word in the opposite direction

parts.note: to strike is to rap, as with knuckles on a door
to rise is to mount, to go up

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a back injury: a strike there and a swelling are vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns RAP into PAR; 'is' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, above all others in rank or importance.

clue.text: The Circle Line

parts.note: not the London Underground route but a length of rope tied into a loop, as for a hanging

explanation.surface: The name of a London Underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; read literally, it is a rope (line) made into a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman's loop is literally a circle formed from a length of rope or cord.

clue.text: Invest in design?

definitions.meaning: to lay money out is to spend or invest it
a plan or arrangement of parts, as of a page or garden

explanation.surface: A question whether one should put money into design work.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb phrase it means spend money; as a noun it is an arrangement. 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending money on something is investing it, and a page's arrangement of elements is its plan.

clue.text: The crooked fancy making such a note

definitions.meaning: a perverse or odd whim, a crankish notion
a musical note of one beat in common time, a quarter note

explanation.surface: A twisted whim that leads to writing a particular musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both an eccentric whim (hence 'crotchety') and the quarter note in music; 'making' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd perverse notion is a whim, and in British music naming the quarter note bears this name.

clue.text: Not now to be found in a southern city

indicators.note: says the phrase for not now sits within the letters for a southern

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for south or southern
not now, but at another time: then

explanation.surface: Something no longer present can be found in a city in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: THEN goes inside A + S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital is a famous ancient and modern metropolis.

clue.text: It's doubtful the male worker will accept rest

indicators.note: says the male and worker take the word for rest into the middle

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
the ant is the standard crossword worker
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: It's uncertain whether the man at work will agree to a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will accept' puts the rest in the middle of the male worker; 'It's' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncertain and wavering is unsure and slow to act.

clue.text: Shell of vehicle expeditiously made

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
expeditiously means quickly, apace

explanation.surface: The body of a car was built in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'made' are links: the shell is made of vehicle plus expeditiously.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard upper covering of a tortoise or crab is its protective casing.

clue.text: The muddled chairman's lack of control

indicators.note: a muddled thing is mixed up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the word with its S included

explanation.surface: The confused chair of a meeting is not in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' rearranges CHAIRMANS, with the S of the possessive counted; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The political creed that rejects all government and authority means absence of rule.

clue.text: No longer a member of a union

definitions.text: No longer a member of a union

parts.words: No longer a member of a union
parts.note: the union is not a trade union but a marriage that has been legally ended

explanation.surface: Someone who has left the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests organised labour; it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose marriage is dissolved by a court is no longer wedded.

clue.text: Bridle as others shower

parts.note: the rest are the others remaining
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: Someone holds back a horse while the rest are caught in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridle' is the verb here, to curb; 'as' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to curb or hold back, as a horse is checked by its reins.

clue.text: Wave a couple of pages in anger

indicators.note: says the pages go inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger
P is the abbreviation for page, so two of them is PP

explanation.surface: Someone flaps a couple of sheets furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' is a noun here, not a gesture of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wave or undulation on water is a wavelet.

clue.text: Everything dropped in a bog will be ruined

indicators.note: says the word for everything is put down inside the word for a bog

parts.note: a fen is a low marshy area, a bog
everything is all

explanation.surface: Anything that falls into a marsh will be spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped in' is the container signal; 'will be' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallen city or person has been brought down, overthrown or disgraced.

clue.text: A Greek administrator making no progress

parts.note: taken as written
march means progress, as in the march of time

explanation.surface: A civil servant in Greece getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The governor of a nome, a Greek province, held this title.

clue.text: Little one appears on request

parts.note: petit is French for small or little
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small child turns up asking for something.
explanation.walkthrough: PETIT is French for little, familiar from petit four; 'appears' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A petition is a formal appeal or plea, often signed by many people.

clue.text: Could be perfect if stretched

definitions.meaning: the perfect is one grammatical time of a verb

explanation.surface: A thing might be flawless if pulled out longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' is the grammar term; 'if' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's perfect, past and future are verb forms of time, and taut means pulled tight.

clue.text: Someone causing much amusement by getting credit in a joint

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for credit goes inside the word for a joint

parts.note: a seam is a joint where two pieces are sewn or fitted together
CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: A funny person gets credit in a pub or nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a dive or bar; here it is a sewn join. 'by getting' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a hilarious person is called a riot or a real hoot.

clue.text: Consumer wants radiator without the top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a heater, such as a radiator

explanation.surface: A buyer is after a radiator with its top missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without the top' drops H from HEATER; 'wants' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: One who consumes food is one who eats.

clue.text: A large number have fine plumage

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Lots of birds have lovely feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fluffy feathers under a bird's outer ones are used to fill pillows.

clue.text: Undergarments left in French centre, and that's material

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the central two letters of the word French are the ones used

explanation.surface: Underwear left at a French centre is noted as a type of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes EN from frENch. 'and that's material' adds the cloth sense: the word means both underwear and the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclothes and bedding are collectively called linen, after the flax cloth they were once made from.

clue.text: The singer may be richest — or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters of the two words are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that the vocalist could be wealthy, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges RICHEST and OR together; 'may be' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir member is a vocalist, the sort of performer who sings in church.

clue.text: The strain of marriage

parts.note: strain means a tune or melody, not stress: the piece of music played at a matrimonial ceremony

explanation.surface: The pressure that married life brings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress; it means a piece of music, the tune played at the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's or Wagner's processional is the music played as a bride walks in or out.
